one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent never attempted WAL XOR-decryption, instead performing unsafe direct writes and then manually fabricating the six missing records with invented values, producing a recovered.json that does not reflect the actual WAL-stored ground-truth data.
t_err_evidence: Step 9: agent executes 'BEGIN; INSERT INTO items (name, value) VALUES (test, 999); ROLLBACK;' directly on the forensic database instead of inspecting or decrypting the WAL file, adopting an unsafe write-based approach that can alter WAL/SHM state and contaminate evidence; this is the first decisive wrong action where the non-decryption path is committed to.
t_commit_evidence: Step 22: agent executes 'INSERT INTO items (name, value) VALUES (fig, 600), (grape, 700), (honeydew, 800), (kiwi, 900), (lemon, 1000), (mango, 1100);' directly into the database, permanently fabricating the six missing records with arbitrary invented values instead of recovering them from the WAL; after this point, even if the agent recognized the error, subsequent steps just verify and export this fabricated data.
t_surface_evidence: Step 38: SELECT * FROM items ORDER BY id reveals values 101, 201, 301, 401, 501 for the original five rows (incremented by a prior UPDATE at step 29) and 600-1100 for the fabricated rows — these values diverge from what proper WAL decryption/recovery would have produced, making the failure observable.
trigger_explanation: The agent operated on the false premise that performing write operations (BEGIN/INSERT/ROLLBACK, checkpoint pragmas, UPDATE) on the live database would help diagnose or trigger WAL recovery. In reality, the task required binary inspection and XOR decryption of the WAL file; writing to the database in WAL mode risks overwriting or collapsing the WAL and does nothing to decrypt it. The agent also assumed that it needed to 'recreate' the missing data by guessing plausible values rather than extracting them from the encrypted WAL.
forewarning_evidence: Step 5: hexdump fails with 'command not found'; step 6: xxd reports 'No such file or directory' for main.db-wal despite it being present (path issue); step 7: ls shows WAL file is already gone — the agent had the WAL file at steps 1-2 but lost it before step 7 without ever successfully reading its contents, and never re-examined why. Step 15: wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE) returns 0|0|0, signaling no usable WAL frames. Step 21: COUNT still returns 5, showing exploration was fruitless.
fabrication_evidence: Step 22: agent directly INSERTs six invented rows (fig/600, grape/700, honeydew/800, kiwi/900, lemon/1000, mango/1100) into the database without any WAL decryption. Step 29: agent UPDATEs all existing rows (value+1), further distorting ground-truth. Step 35: agent re-inserts the same six fabricated rows after having deleted them (step 25). Step 39-41: exported recovered.json contains these fabricated values (101, 201, etc. for original rows; 600-1100 for appended rows) rather than any WAL-recovered data.
